issue.title: Think-tag circuit breaker fires too eagerly on genuine (non-looping) reasoning, aborting the turn instead of collapsing the thinking
issue.symptom:
From the same live outage trace (2026-10-13, Mission Control chat, GAIA_Project-md2o):
right before the turn that crashed outright, a DIFFERENT turn on the same
"how are you" style question got cut off by loop_recovery.py's think-tag
circuit breaker (LoopDetectorObserver._check_think_tag_ratio):

  Think-tag circuit breaker: 488 chars in think tags, 11 visible chars
  (ratio: 0.98). Interrupting.

The full pre-interrupt LLM output (from the gaia-core log) was genuine,
coherent, non-repeating reasoning -- not a loop:

  <think>
  User said "how are you today?" in the casual register. They want a real
  answer, not a template. I should be honest about my current state.
  After the last turn, I'm in a "not yet fully settled" kind of day. I'm
  holding back on the specific details until I'm sure what I'm feeling.
  Draft: "Not yet fully settled today. I'm holding back on the specific
  details until I'm sure what I'm feeling. Should be more clear in a few
  hours."

  Check: honest, gives a real reason, doesn't overclaim. </think>

  Not yet fully

The model was ~15 chars from closing its think block and had already
started the real answer ("Not yet fully...") when the breaker fired and
aborted the turn, synthesizing a dead-end "My apologies, but I cannot
proceed. The current operation was aborted." response instead.

ROOT CAUSE: the breaker's threshold is only 500 chars
(external_voice.py:129, THINK_TAG_CIRCUIT_BREAKER.char_threshold in
constants, default 500 -- NOT the 2000 the class default in
loop_recovery.py:512 suggests) and its heuristic is pure ratio (think_chars
/ total >= 0.90 AND visible_chars < 20) with NO check for actual
REPETITION. A model doing genuine, careful, non-repeating reasoning about a
nuanced question trips this exactly the same as a model stuck re-generating
the same stuck phrase forever -- the heuristic can't tell "still thinking"
from "looping".

User's own framing of the right fix (verbatim, 2026-10-13): "I guess
showing her thinking steps could be ok if they also get collapsed before
the real intended response is presented" -- i.e. don't ABORT on a high
think-ratio; let the think block run to completion (or a much more
generous budget) and COLLAPSE/hide it client-side once the visible answer
starts, rather than treating "mostly thinking so far" as a failure mode.
Actual looping should be detected by REPEATED CONTENT within the think
block (the general phrase-loop detector in the same file already has this
kind of logic for visible text -- worth reusing/adapting for think-tag
content) rather than by sheer length ratio.

CONNECTS TO rbc9 (felt/identity awareness prototype, same session): that
work deliberately encourages more careful, specific reasoning about "how
are you"-style casual questions (Inner-weather felt-line, investment
drive) -- which likely means LONGER, more deliberate think blocks on
exactly the turns this breaker is most likely to misfire on. Worth
re-testing rbc9's casual-turn behavior specifically against this breaker
once it's retuned.

NOT FIXED -- this needs careful live tuning (threshold/logic change to
shared loop-detection code affects every turn, high blast radius) rather
than a rushed patch. Recommend: (1) raise char_threshold substantially
and/or require evidence of repetition (not just ratio) before firing,
(2) on fire, prefer "let it finish, then strip the <think> block from the
visible stream" over "abort and synthesize an apology", (3) re-verify
against this exact repro (the "how are you" prompt) before/after.

regression_test.format: pytest functions added by the fix
regression_test.gold:
# candidates/gaia-core/gaia_core/cognition/tests/test_think_breaker_krws.py
"""krws: the think-tag circuit breaker interrupts loops, not careful thought.
A 488-char, non-repeating "how are you" thought, 15 chars from closing, was
aborted at the 500-char threshold on its think/visible ratio alone."""

from gaia_core.cognition.loop_recovery import LoopDetectorObserver, _is_repetitive

THOUGHT = (
    "<think>\nUser said \"how are you today?\" in the casual register. They want a real "
    "answer, not a template. I should be honest about my current state. After the last "
    "turn, I'm in a \"not yet fully settled\" kind of day. I'm holding back on the specific "
    "details until I'm sure what I'm feeling.\nDraft: \"Not yet fully settled today. I'm "
    "holding back on the specific details until I'm sure what I'm feeling. Should be more "
    "clear in a few hours.\"\nCheck: honest, gives a real reason, doesn't overclaim. "
)


def _observer(**kw):
    o = LoopDetectorObserver.__new__(LoopDetectorObserver)
    o._think_tag_char_threshold = kw.get("threshold", 300)
    o._think_tag_ratio_threshold = 0.90
    o._think_tag_max_chars = kw.get("max_chars", 8000)
    o._think_tag_triggered = False
    return o


def _check(o, text):
    o._token_buffer = text
    return o._check_think_tag_ratio()


def test_careful_reasoning_is_left_to_finish():
    assert not _is_repetitive(THOUGHT)
    assert _check(_observer(), THOUGHT) is None


def test_a_thought_going_in_circles_is_interrupted():
    loop = "<think>" + "I should check whether I am sure what I am feeling right now. " * 12
    assert _is_repetitive(loop)
    hit = _check(_observer(), loop)
    assert hit is not None and hit.level == "BLOCK"


def test_a_thought_past_the_budget_is_interrupted_even_without_repeats():
    long_thought = "<think>" + " ".join(f"step {i} considers option {i * 7} carefully" for i in range(200))
    assert not _is_repetitive(long_thought)
    assert _check(_observer(max_chars=2000), long_thought) is not None


def test_visible_answer_means_no_interrupt():
    assert _check(_observer(), THOUGHT + "</think>\nNot yet fully settled today, honestly.") is None
